There is a functoriality property for the constructions explained
in Lemmas <REF_0001> and
<REF_0002>. Namely, suppose given
two collections of data <MATH_0001> and
<MATH_0002> as in Lemma <REF_0003>.
Suppose for every <MATH_0003> given
a morphism <MATH_0004> over <MATH_0005> compatible with
the restrictions <MATH_0006> and <MATH_0007>. Functoriality
means that this gives rise to a morphism of schemes
<MATH_0008> over <MATH_0009> restricting back to the morphisms <MATH_0010>,
where <MATH_0011> is obtained from
the datum <MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013>
is obtained from the datum <MATH_0014>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Similarly, suppose given
two collections of data
<MATH_0015> and
<MATH_0016>
as in Lemma <REF_0004>.
Suppose for every <MATH_0017> given
a morphism <MATH_0018> over <MATH_0019> compatible with
the restrictions <MATH_0020> and <MATH_0021>, and a morphism
<MATH_0022> compatible with
the maps <MATH_0023> and <MATH_0024>. Functoriality
means that these give rise to a morphism of schemes
<MATH_0025> over <MATH_0026> restricting back to the morphisms <MATH_0027>,
and a morphism <MATH_0028> restricting back
to the maps <MATH_0029>
where <MATH_0030> is obtained from the datum
<MATH_0031> and
where <MATH_0032> is obtained from the datum
<MATH_0033>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
We omit the verifications and we omit a suitable formulation of
``equivalence of categories'' between relative glueing data
and relative objects.
